subject.title: fix #95279: Provide a trusted inbound-decoration contract so consumers can strip/dedup without forgeable text heuristics

question: Should the durable trusted inbound-decoration contract be an OpenClaw-owned namespaced message-metadata field written by the decoration owner, rather than the proposed generic top-level `bareBody` and `inboundDecorated` fields?
rationale: This decides the permanent serialized/runtime ownership boundary across transcripts, UI, memory, CLI history, and plugins; it cannot be safely inferred from a contributor patch.

options.title: Adopt namespaced host metadata
options.body: Define one `__openclaw`-owned inbound-decoration record, populate it at the actual decoration producer, and update readers to consume only that record.

options.title: Accept generic top-level fields
options.body: Keep the proposed top-level fields, but explicitly document and approve them as a supported generic message contract with provenance and compatibility tests.

options.title: Pause the contract change
options.body: Keep legacy stripping until maintainers choose a durable ownership boundary and source-of-truth producer.

recommendation.title: Adopt namespaced host metadata
recommendation.body: Define one `__openclaw`-owned inbound-decoration record, populate it at the actual decoration producer, and update readers to consume only that record.

likelyOwner.reason: They supplied the canonical problem statement and can provide the most direct context on the required lossless behavior, although code-owner routing remains low confidence.
